concepts.def: The peak at highest m/z in a mass spectrum, formed by the intact ionised molecule, gives the relative molecular mass.
Molecular ions break apart in the spectrometer; fragment peaks such as m/z 15 for CH₃⁺ identify pieces of the structure.
IR radiation makes covalent bonds vibrate; absorptions at characteristic wavenumbers identify functional groups such as O–H and C=O.
The position of a proton NMR signal shows the chemical environment of the hydrogen atoms, measured relative to TMS at zero.
A ¹H NMR signal splits into n + 1 lines when there are n hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms.
In chromatography, Rf equals the distance moved by the spot divided by the distance moved by the solvent front.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Modern Analytical Techniques — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Modern Analytical Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Modern Analytical Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In a mass spectrum, the molecular ion peak gives:
options: The relative molecular mass
The most stable fragment
The number of carbon atoms
The boiling point

mcqs.q: A very broad IR absorption from 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ together with a strong C=O peak suggests:
options: A carboxylic acid
An alkane
An ether
An alkene

mcqs.q: In ¹H NMR, a quartet arises from coupling to how many protons on the adjacent carbon?
A fragment peak 15 units below the molecular ion usually shows loss of:
options: CH₃
OH
C₂H₅
H₂O

mcqs.q: Is the tallest peak in a mass spectrum the molecular ion?
options: The molecular ion always appears at exactly m/z = 100.
Not necessarily — the tallest (base) peak is just the most abundant ion; the molecular ion is the highest m/z peak and is often small.
The molecular ion is always the biggest peak in the spectrum.
IR spectroscopy works by breaking the bonds and weighing the fragments.

mcqs.q: Does an IR spectrum identify a whole molecule on its own?
options: Each molecule shows one single IR peak that names it directly.
The number of NMR signals equals the number of carbon atoms.
It mainly identifies functional groups from bond vibrations; confirming the full structure usually needs the fingerprint region or other techniques like NMR and mass spectrometry.
IR spectroscopy works by breaking the bonds and weighing the fragments.

mcqs.q: In ¹H NMR, does the number of signals equal the number of hydrogen atoms?
options: The molecular ion always appears at exactly m/z = 100.
The number of NMR signals equals the number of carbon atoms.
No — the number of signals equals the number of distinct hydrogen environments; equivalent hydrogens contribute to one signal.
A molecule with six hydrogens always shows six NMR signals.
